newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: 11 countries tune out as U.N. proclaims World TV Day.
newsitem.headline: 11 countries tune out as U.N. proclaims World TV Day.

text.p: The United States and 10 other countries tuned out on Tuesday when the General Assembly, by a vote of 141 to 0 with 11 abstentions, proclaimed Nov. 21 as World Television Day.
That was the date the first World Television Forum was held at the United Nations, sponsored by Italian State Television, the Italian government and the U.N. department of public information.
The resolution proclaiming the annual observance was sponsored by Italy joined by 146 other countries -- more than the number who finally voted for it.

Letitia Chambers of the United States, explaining her abstention, called the proclamation a "doubtful expenditure of time and energy, at best" since other resolutions already addressed substantive issues surrounding the communication of U.N. activities.

She also said a commemorative day not organized around the concept of the free and uncensored flow of information and ideas ran the risk of "providing legitimacy for those who would misuse television as a tool of repression and control."

A German representative, who also abstained, noted the United Nations already celebrated an annual World Press Freedom Day (May 3), World Telecommunication Day (May 17) and World Development Information Day (Oct. 24). Also abstaining were: Britain, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Haiti, Japan, Netherlands, Norway and Sweden.
